detailedSolution:

For Syllabus Core (History of Buddhism and Jainism (Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings)):
In the Agganna Sutta of the Sutta Pitaka, early Buddhism outlines a social contract theory of kingship: as human society degenerated through greed and conflict, the people gathered and decided to choose an upright person to dispense justice in return for a fraction of their paddy. questionText:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Names) List-II (Associations)
(A) Piyadassi
(I) Script
(B) Kalinga
(II) Reporter
(C) Kharosthi
(III) Asoka
(D) Pativedaka (IV) Coastal Orissa
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Syllabus Core.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Syllabus Core (History of Buddhism and Jainism (Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings)):
Epigraphic terms: 'Piyadassi' (pleasant to behold) was the standard honorific title used by Emperor Asoka in his rock and pillar edicts (A-(III)). Kalinga was the ancient name for coastal Odisha conquered in Ashoka's eighth regnal year (B-(IV)). Kharosthi was the right-to-left script used for Ashokan edicts in the northwest (C-(I)). In Major Rock Edict VI, Ashoka commanded the 'pativedakas' (special reporters) to report public affairs to him at all times and places (D-(II)). Match: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
